correctness.rationale: By Fourier inversion the fixed-window energy is the real sinc quadratic form, whose off-diagonal pairwise sign must be saturated by any universal phase: two shrinking independent nonnegative packets expose any violating pair. Locally positive sinc kernel forces almost-everywhere constant phase per connected band. Any scaled width >1 conflicts with a negative in-band sinc lobe. Cross-band differences of gap r occupy intervals centred r x with maximal half-width Delta_r; continuity of their sign and adjacent band parity require floor(r {x}) to be even for all r. The floor staircase increments by 0 or 1 and begins 0, hence stays 0, yielding sharp Delta_r <= r {x} <= 1-Delta_r. Conversely those inequalities make signed sinc kernel pointwise nonnegative under the proposed alternating phase, proving universal optimality and uniqueness, including measure-zero zeros at closed endpoints. Independent 7000 deterministic sampled sign tests compared the criterion to all pairwise lobe signs; finite tests are corroboration only. One printed theorem line has a harmless notation typo nu instead of u; the proof unambiguously defines u=x-floor x.
